newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to auction 36-month NTN-Ds on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to auction 36-month NTN-Ds on Friday.

text.p: The National Treasury said it will auction 300 million reais of dollar-indexed (NTN-D) notes on Friday as part of an ongoing bid to lengthen maturities on Brazil's massive domestic debt.
"For the first time the auction includes three-year paper. This is part of a strategy to extend public debt maturities," Treasury Secretary Eduardo Guimaraes said in a statement.
The longest maturity on dollar-indexed Treasury paper is now 24 months.

At Friday's auction, to be held about 1130 local/1330 GMT, the Treasury will also auction 400 million reais of 24-month NTN-Ds, and 800 million reais of six-month NTN-H notes, which are indexed to the Central Bank's reference rate TR.
In addition, the Treasury will offer 2.8 billion reais in 181-day letters (LTN) and 5.3 billion reais in 365-day letters.
Results of the auction are due at about 1530 local/1730 GMT.

Aside from lengthening debt maturities, the new 36-month dollar-indexed issue is also designed to reassure futures markets that the Central Bank will not alter its exchange rate policy, according to currency and debt traders.
Currently, the Central Bank depreciates reais by between 0.55 percent and 0.65 percent each month.
But futures markets have speculated about a faster rate of devaluation because of fears over Brazil's swelling trade deficit.
If policy-makers did speed depreciation, holders of NTN-Ds are protected because the notes pay a fixed rate plus the variation in the foreign exchange rate.
